breakfast.name: Nasi Lemak (Coconut Rice)
breakfast.description: Malaysian coconut rice with anchovies, peanuts, and boiled eggs
instructions: Cook rice with coconut milk, water, pandan leaves
Heat oil, fry garlic until golden
Prepare toppings: fry anchovies, roast peanuts
Top with anchovies, peanuts, cucumber, egg
Serve with sambal on the side
breakfast.fun_fact: Nasi Lemak is Malaysia's national breakfast and is served everywhere from hawker stalls to hotels

lunch.name: Laksa (Spicy Noodle Soup)
lunch.description: Malaysian spicy coconut noodle soup with shrimp and fish cake
ingredients: Paste: 6 dried chilies, 4 cloves garlic, 1-inch turmeric, 1-inch galangal, 3 stalks lemongrass, 1 tbsp shrimp paste
instructions: Heat oil in pot, fry paste 3 minutes
Garnish with lime juice and herbs
lunch.notes: Paste must be fragrant before adding liquids
lunch.fun_fact: Laksa is beloved across Malaysia and has regional variations in each state

dinner.name: Rendang Lemak (Rich Coconut Curry)
dinner.description: Malaysian rich coconut curry with vegetables and meat
ingredients: Paste: shallots, garlic, chilies, galangal, turmeric, lemongrass
instructions: Heat oil, fry paste until fragrant
Meat should be tender and sauce thick
dinner.notes: Low and slow cooking is essential
dinner.fun_fact: Rendang Lemak is a festive dish served at Malaysian celebrations

snacks.name: Kuih Lapis (Layered Cake)
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt
Add different food colors to each part
Add pandan extract to one part
Mix each with coconut milk and eggs
Pour colored batter layers into greased steamer pan
Steam each layer 3-5 minutes before adding next
Steam completely at the end 10 minutes
snacks.fun_fact: Kuih Lapis is an elaborate Malaysian delicacy often made for special occasions

desserts.name: Cendol (Sweet Dessert Drink)
desserts.description: Malaysian sweet pandan noodle dessert with gula melaka syrup
instructions: Make gula melaka syrup: melt palm sugar in water
desserts.notes: Cendol must be chewy and fresh
desserts.fun_fact: Cendol is one of Malaysia's most beloved desserts and is sold throughout the country

nonAlcoholicDrinks.name: Teh Tarik (Pulled Tea)
nonAlcoholicDrinks.description: Malaysian strong tea pulled high from pot to create foam
instructions: Brew strong tea in small pot
Hold cup high and pour between cups repeatedly
nonAlcoholicDrinks.notes: The pouring action is an art form
nonAlcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Teh Tarik is Malaysia's national drink and the pouring technique is performed with flair at street stalls

alcoholicDrinks.name: Malaysian Beer
alcoholicDrinks.description: Light lager beer popular in Malaysia
alcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Beer consumption in Malaysia is increasing despite being a Muslim-majority country
